![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071601/assets/d1bc2b703c1d73e735bdbb1d2abab86f86447e87fbeabde57126114726f78757.png)
Consider the matrix $P$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $A=PCP^{-1},$ what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
e-5531.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2 \times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PCP^{-1},$ where 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071601/assets/558cbc7aba862d44e34a7b109ea84c1f7a6f3f1f4b505e5f476e62a29fdd654b.png)

and $\mathbf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda.$

- From the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071601/assets/ca2243ed8015927b9db5428d676ee59907264fc223721246a81b2e73aca3b351.png) we deduce that $\textrm{Re}(\lambda)={\color{blue}3}$ and $\textrm{Im}(\lambda) = {\color{red}-1}.$ So, our eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda = {\color{blue}3}+({\color{red}-1})\text{i} = 3-\text{i}.
$$

- From the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071601/assets/7a5bb57b71eb218271f2bb0ab718304d6b834738f1004eac7c501a7fd4ffa2b3.png) we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071601/assets/0ea51255e7594236cdd5d8dee0997f64b49f77cbb77e8cfd97937830a862283b.png)

Finally, the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda,$ and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of $\mathbf{v}.$

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are

e-5530.knowledge_point: Converting a Matrix to Rotation-Scaling Form Given Multiple Parts of the Decomposition
e-5530.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071601/assets/5f3cd6aeb514ee0a59d1f3534342f85e1c00743d9e7c7004b8aaf8ccfbe353f9.png)
Consider the vector $\mathbf{v}$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $\mathbf{v}$ is an eigenvector of a $2 \times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda=-1-4\textrm{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PCP^{-1}.$
e-5530.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2 \times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PCP^{-1},$ where 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071601/assets/9fb15e52a1df912c9e5fb4238f45d705cd0a56fb7190620c0f0fd597f9a2b8c0.png)

and $\mathbf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda.$

First, notice that 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071601/assets/80bd36915851e6ebeb67befe8af41e5496fa5491b9d87c294d8b937eb586319f.png)

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

e-8734.knowledge_point: Converting a Matrix to Rotation-Scaling Form Using the Complex Conjugate
e-8734.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071601/assets/f4a051da70308d92a5530fca3ba9c214cff919a6072e0e4d863f5aad10f405ee.png)
Consider the vector $\mathbf{v}$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $\mathbf{v}$ is an eigenvector of a $2 \times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda=2+4\textrm{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PCP^{-1}.$
e-8734.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2 \times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PCP^{-1},$ where 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071601/assets/4a53548a17d9b4fd870ce70285bfc2c57cf6c8d352f75149e5aa7511ef4af853.png)

and $\mathbf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda.$

First, notice that 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071601/assets/aa5738b600440bf8327670fc21cd8005c660def232119b2b4808237d988367bd.png)

while

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071601/assets/fc91fcabd47720075061e670f62be9ea9b636070a05cba70752bb7060608b764.png)

So, our rotation-scaling matrix $C$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\overline{\lambda}=2-4\textrm{i},$ 
 the complex conjugate of $\lambda.$ Hence, to construct the matrix $P,$ we use the eigenvector $\overline{\mathbf{v}},$ the complex conjugate of $\mathbf{v}.$

Next, we find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{v} & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} \\ 7\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(\overset{―}{v})}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(\overset{―}{v})}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(\overset{―}{v}) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{v}) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

P=[305−2],C=[−2−11−2] Consider the matrix P and the rotation-scaling matrix C shown above. Given that A=PCP−1, what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=5∓2i and v=[3−2∓i]
b
λ=1∓2i and v=[35∓2i]
c
λ=−2∓i and v=[35∓2i]
d
λ=1∓2i and v=[31∓2i]
e
λ=−2∓i and v=[32∓5i]
Submit

decision.explanation: C has eigenvalue -2-i with eigenvector (1,i)^T. Multiplying by P gives the corresponding eigenvector of A: P(1,i)^T=(3,5-2i)^T. Complex conjugation gives the other pair, -2+i and (3,5+2i)^T. Thus option c is correct.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

- From the matrix $C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ -(-1) & -2\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that $\text{Re}(\lambda )=-2$ and $\text{Im}(\lambda )=-1.$ So, our eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda =-2+(-1)\text{i}=-2-\text{i}.
$$

- From the matrix $P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}3+0\text{i} \\ 5+(-2)\text{i}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda ,$ and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of $v.$

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are 

$$
\lambda =-2∓\text{i},\,v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5∓2\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 1
?

P=[305−2],C=[−2−11−2] Consider the matrix P and the rotation-scaling matrix C shown above. Given that A=PCP−1, what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=5∓2i and v=[3−2∓i]
b
λ=1∓2i and v=[35∓2i]
c
λ=−2∓i and v=[35∓2i]
d
λ=1∓2i and v=[31∓2i]
e
λ=−2∓i and v=[32∓5i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that for any 2×2 real matrix A with complex eigenvalues, we have A=PCP−1, where

P=[||Re(v)Im(v)||],C=[Re(λ)Im(λ)−Im(λ)Re(λ)],

and v is an eigenvector of A corresponding to the complex eigenvalue λ.

  • From the matrix C=[−2−1−(−1)−2], we deduce that Re(λ)=−2 and Im(λ)=−1. So, our eigenvalue is λ=−2+(−1)i=−2−i.

  • From the matrix P=[305−2], we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is v=[3+0i5+(−2)i]=[35−2i].

Finally, the second eigenvalue of A must be the complex conjugate of λ, and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of v.

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are

λ=−2∓i,v=[35∓2i].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors of a Matrix in Rotation-Scaling Form
content.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

- From the matrix $C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ -(-1) & -2\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that $\text{Re}(\lambda )=-2$ and $\text{Im}(\lambda )=-1.$ So, our eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda =-2+(-1)\text{i}=-2-\text{i}.
$$

- From the matrix $P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}3+0\text{i} \\ 5+(-2)\text{i}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda ,$ and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of $v.$

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are 

$$
\lambda =-2∓\text{i},\,v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5∓2\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 2
?

P=[−1430],C=[5−225] Consider the matrix P and the rotation-scaling matrix C shown above. Given that A=PCP−1, what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=5∓2i and v=[−1±4i3]
b
λ=−1±4i and v=[5±2i3]
c
λ=2±5i and v=[−1±4i3]
d
λ=5∓2i and v=[4±i3]
e
λ=−1∓4i and v=[2±5i3]
Submit

decision.explanation: C(1,i)^T=(5-2i)(1,i)^T, so A has eigenvalue 5-2i with eigenvector P(1,i)^T=(-1+4i,3)^T. Conjugation gives eigenvalue 5+2i with eigenvector (-1-4i,3)^T. These paired signs match option a.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

- From the matrix $C=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -(-2) & 5\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that $\text{Re}(\lambda )=5$ and $\text{Im}(\lambda )=-2.$ So, our eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda =5+(-2)\text{i}=5-2\text{i}.
$$

- From the matrix $P=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1+4\text{i} \\ 3+0\text{i}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1+4\text{i} \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda ,$ and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of $v.$

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are 

$$
\lambda =5∓2\text{i},\,v=[\begin{aligned}-1\pm 4\text{i} \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 2
?

P=[−1430],C=[5−225] Consider the matrix P and the rotation-scaling matrix C shown above. Given that A=PCP−1, what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=5∓2i and v=[−1±4i3]
b
λ=−1±4i and v=[5±2i3]
c
λ=2±5i and v=[−1±4i3]
d
λ=5∓2i and v=[4±i3]
e
λ=−1∓4i and v=[2±5i3]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that for any 2×2 real matrix A with complex eigenvalues, we have A=PCP−1, where

P=[||Re(v)Im(v)||],C=[Re(λ)Im(λ)−Im(λ)Re(λ)],

and v is an eigenvector of A corresponding to the complex eigenvalue λ.

  • From the matrix C=[5−2−(−2)5], we deduce that Re(λ)=5 and Im(λ)=−2. So, our eigenvalue is λ=5+(−2)i=5−2i.

  • From the matrix P=[−1430], we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is v=[−1+4i3+0i]=[−1+4i3].

Finally, the second eigenvalue of A must be the complex conjugate of λ, and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of v.

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are

λ=5∓2i,v=[−1±4i3].

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option a: 5-2i corresponds to (-1+4i,3)^T, and conjugation gives 5+2i with (-1-4i,3)^T. Directly, C(1,i)^T=(5-2i)(1,i)^T and P(1,i)^T=(-1+4i,3)^T. The displayed incorrect result concerns the deliberately submitted option e.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors of a Matrix in Rotation-Scaling Form
content.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

- From the matrix $C=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -(-2) & 5\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that $\text{Re}(\lambda )=5$ and $\text{Im}(\lambda )=-2.$ So, our eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda =5+(-2)\text{i}=5-2\text{i}.
$$

- From the matrix $P=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1+4\text{i} \\ 3+0\text{i}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1+4\text{i} \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda ,$ and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of $v.$

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are 

$$
\lambda =5∓2\text{i},\,v=[\begin{aligned}-1\pm 4\text{i} \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 3

P=[41−3−1],C=[0−220] Consider the matrix P and the rotation-scaling matrix C shown above. Given that A=PCP−1, what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=4∓i and v=[±2i−3∓i]
b
λ=2∓i and v=[4±i∓2i]
c
λ=2∓i and v=[4±i−3∓i]
d
λ=∓2i and v=[4±i−3∓i]
e
λ=∓2i and v=[2±i1∓i]
Submit

decision.explanation: C(1,i)^T=-2i(1,i)^T, so the corresponding eigenvector of A is P(1,i)^T=(4+i,-3-i)^T. Taking conjugates gives eigenvalue 2i with eigenvector (4-i,-3+i)^T. These pairs match option d.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

- From the matrix $C=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -(-2) & 0\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that $\text{Re}(\lambda )=0$ and $\text{Im}(\lambda )=-2.$ So, our eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda =0+(-2)\text{i}=-2\text{i}.
$$

- From the matrix $P=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}4+1\text{i} \\ -3+(-1)\text{i}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4+\text{i} \\ -3-\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda ,$ and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of $v.$

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are 

$$
\lambda =∓2\text{i},\,v=[\begin{aligned}4\pm \text{i} \\ -3∓\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 3
?

P=[41−3−1],C=[0−220] Consider the matrix P and the rotation-scaling matrix C shown above. Given that A=PCP−1, what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=4∓i and v=[±2i−3∓i]
b
λ=2∓i and v=[4±i∓2i]
c
λ=2∓i and v=[4±i−3∓i]
d
λ=∓2i and v=[4±i−3∓i]
e
λ=∓2i and v=[2±i1∓i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that for any 2×2 real matrix A with complex eigenvalues, we have A=PCP−1, where

P=[||Re(v)Im(v)||],C=[Re(λ)Im(λ)−Im(λ)Re(λ)],

and v is an eigenvector of A corresponding to the complex eigenvalue λ.

  • From the matrix C=[0−2−(−2)0], we deduce that Re(λ)=0 and Im(λ)=−2. So, our eigenvalue is λ=0+(−2)i=−2i.

  • From the matrix P=[41−3−1], we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is v=[4+1i−3+(−1)i]=[4+i−3−i].

Finally, the second eigenvalue of A must be the complex conjugate of λ, and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of v.

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are

λ=∓2i,v=[4±i−3∓i].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors of a Matrix in Rotation-Scaling Form
content.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

- From the matrix $C=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -(-2) & 0\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that $\text{Re}(\lambda )=0$ and $\text{Im}(\lambda )=-2.$ So, our eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda =0+(-2)\text{i}=-2\text{i}.
$$

- From the matrix $P=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}4+1\text{i} \\ -3+(-1)\text{i}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4+\text{i} \\ -3-\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda ,$ and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of $v.$

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are 

$$
\lambda =∓2\text{i},\,v=[\begin{aligned}4\pm \text{i} \\ -3∓\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 4
?

P=[0120],C=[1−221] Consider the matrix P and the rotation-scaling matrix C shown above. Given that A=PCP−1, what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=±2i and v=[±i0]
b
λ=−1∓2i and v=[±i−2]
c
λ=2±i and v=[2±i]
d
λ=1∓2i and v=[±i1]
e
λ=1∓2i and v=[±i2]
Submit

decision.explanation: C(1,i)^T=(1-2i)(1,i)^T, and P(1,i)^T=(i,2)^T. Thus 1-2i corresponds to (i,2)^T; conjugation gives 1+2i with (-i,2)^T. These pairs match option e.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

- From the matrix $C=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -(-2) & 1\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that $\text{Re}(\lambda )=1$ and $\text{Im}(\lambda )=-2.$ So, our eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda =1+(-2)\text{i}=1-2\text{i}.
$$

- From the matrix $P=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}0+1\text{i} \\ 2+0\text{i}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda ,$ and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of $v.$

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are 

$$
\lambda =1∓2\text{i},\,v=[\begin{aligned}\pm \text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 4
?

P=[0120],C=[1−221] Consider the matrix P and the rotation-scaling matrix C shown above. Given that A=PCP−1, what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=±2i and v=[±i0]
b
λ=−1∓2i and v=[±i−2]
c
λ=2±i and v=[2±i]
d
λ=1∓2i and v=[±i1]
e
λ=1∓2i and v=[±i2]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that for any 2×2 real matrix A with complex eigenvalues, we have A=PCP−1, where

P=[||Re(v)Im(v)||],C=[Re(λ)Im(λ)−Im(λ)Re(λ)],

and v is an eigenvector of A corresponding to the complex eigenvalue λ.

  • From the matrix C=[1−2−(−2)1], we deduce that Re(λ)=1 and Im(λ)=−2. So, our eigenvalue is λ=1+(−2)i=1−2i.

  • From the matrix P=[0120], we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is v=[0+1i2+0i]=[i2].

Finally, the second eigenvalue of A must be the complex conjugate of λ, and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of v.

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are

λ=1∓2i,v=[±i2].

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option e. Since C(1,i)^T=(1-2i)(1,i)^T, multiplying by P gives the eigenvector (i,2)^T of A. Conjugation gives the other pair, 1+2i and (-i,2)^T. The incorrect feedback concerns deliberately submitted option c.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors of a Matrix in Rotation-Scaling Form
content.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

- From the matrix $C=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -(-2) & 1\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that $\text{Re}(\lambda )=1$ and $\text{Im}(\lambda )=-2.$ So, our eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda =1+(-2)\text{i}=1-2\text{i}.
$$

- From the matrix $P=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}0+1\text{i} \\ 2+0\text{i}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda ,$ and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of $v.$

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are 

$$
\lambda =1∓2\text{i},\,v=[\begin{aligned}\pm \text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 5
?

P=[1−2−32],C=[−7−22−7] Consider the matrix P and the rotation-scaling matrix C shown above. Given that A=PCP−1, what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=−7±2i and v=[1±i]
b
λ=−7∓2i and v=[2∓i−3±2i]
c
λ=2∓7i and v=[1∓2i−3±2i]
d
λ=−7∓2i and v=[1∓2i−3±2i]
e
λ=−2∓7i and v=[1∓2i−3∓2i]
Submit

decision.explanation: C(1,i)^T=(-7-2i)(1,i)^T, and P(1,i)^T=(1-2i,-3+2i)^T. Conjugation gives eigenvalue -7+2i with eigenvector (1+2i,-3-2i)^T. These pairs match option d.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -2 \\ 2 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

- From the matrix $C=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -2 \\ -(-2) & -7\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that $\text{Re}(\lambda )=-7$ and $\text{Im}(\lambda )=-2.$ So, our eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda =-7+(-2)\text{i}=-7-2\text{i}.
$$

- From the matrix $P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1+(-2)\text{i} \\ -3+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1-2\text{i} \\ -3+2\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda ,$ and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of $v.$

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are 

$$
\lambda =-7∓2\text{i},\,v=[\begin{aligned}1∓2\text{i} \\ -3\pm 2\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 5
?

P=[1−2−32],C=[−7−22−7] Consider the matrix P and the rotation-scaling matrix C shown above. Given that A=PCP−1, what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=−7±2i and v=[1±i]
b
λ=−7∓2i and v=[2∓i−3±2i]
c
λ=2∓7i and v=[1∓2i−3±2i]
d
λ=−7∓2i and v=[1∓2i−3±2i]
e
λ=−2∓7i and v=[1∓2i−3∓2i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that for any 2×2 real matrix A with complex eigenvalues, we have A=PCP−1, where

P=[||Re(v)Im(v)||],C=[Re(λ)Im(λ)−Im(λ)Re(λ)],

and v is an eigenvector of A corresponding to the complex eigenvalue λ.

  • From the matrix C=[−7−2−(−2)−7], we deduce that Re(λ)=−7 and Im(λ)=−2. So, our eigenvalue is λ=−7+(−2)i=−7−2i.

  • From the matrix P=[1−2−32], we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is v=[1+(−2)i−3+2i]=[1−2i−3+2i].

Finally, the second eigenvalue of A must be the complex conjugate of λ, and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of v.

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are

λ=−7∓2i,v=[1∓2i−3±2i].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors of a Matrix in Rotation-Scaling Form
content.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -2 \\ 2 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

- From the matrix $C=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -2 \\ -(-2) & -7\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that $\text{Re}(\lambda )=-7$ and $\text{Im}(\lambda )=-2.$ So, our eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda =-7+(-2)\text{i}=-7-2\text{i}.
$$

- From the matrix $P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1+(-2)\text{i} \\ -3+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1-2\text{i} \\ -3+2\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda ,$ and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of $v.$

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are 

$$
\lambda =-7∓2\text{i},\,v=[\begin{aligned}1∓2\text{i} \\ -3\pm 2\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

decision.explanation: Use the real and imaginary parts of v as the columns of P. Since Re(v)=(1,2)^T and Im(v)=(2,0)^T, P=[[1,2],[2,0]], whose determinant is -4. This gives the stated rotation-scaling matrix for λ=2-3i and matches option c.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2-3\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Converting a Matrix to Rotation-Scaling Form Given Multiple Parts of the Decomposition
content.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2-3\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2\text{i}-7 \\ 4\text{i}+3\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ -4 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =7+4\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ -4 & 7\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i}-7 \\ 4\text{i}+3\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Recall that for any 2×2 real matrix A with complex eigenvalues, we have A=PCP−1, where

P=[||Re(v)Im(v)||],C=[Re(λ)Im(λ)−Im(λ)Re(λ)],

and v is an eigenvector of A corresponding to the complex eigenvalue λ.

First, notice that

[Re(λ)Im(λ)−Im(λ)Re(λ)]=[74−47]=C.

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

v=[2i−74i+3]=[−73]⏟Re(v)+i[24]⏟Im(v)

Finally, we can now construct P:

P=[||Re(v)Im(v)||]=[−7234].

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms P=[Re(v), Im(v)]=[[-7,2],[3,4]], which is option a. Its determinant is -34, so it is invertible, and the eigenvector equation gives AP=PC. The incorrect feedback concerns deliberately submitted option c.

content.knowledge_point: Converting a Matrix to Rotation-Scaling Form Given Multiple Parts of the Decomposition
content.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2\text{i}-7 \\ 4\text{i}+3\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ -4 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =7+4\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ -4 & 7\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i}-7 \\ 4\text{i}+3\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}5-3\text{i} \\ 2\text{i}-7\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =5+3\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}5-3\text{i} \\ 2\text{i}-7\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Converting a Matrix to Rotation-Scaling Form Given Multiple Parts of the Decomposition
content.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}5-3\text{i} \\ 2\text{i}-7\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =5+3\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}5-3\text{i} \\ 2\text{i}-7\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}7-3\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}7-3\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Converting a Matrix to Rotation-Scaling Form Given Multiple Parts of the Decomposition
content.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}7-3\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}7-3\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3+4\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Converting a Matrix to Rotation-Scaling Form Given Multiple Parts of the Decomposition
content.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3+4\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: C corresponds to the conjugate eigenvalue 3+2i, so use the conjugate vector (2-i,1+i)^T. Its real and imaginary parts give P=[[2,-1],[1,1]], option a. Its determinant is 3, and AP=PC implies A=PCP^{-1}.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2+\text{i} \\ 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3-2\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\ne C,
$$

while

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) \\ -\text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda })\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

So, our rotation-scaling matrix $C$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\overset{―}{\lambda }=3+2\text{i},$ 
 the complex conjugate of $\lambda .$ Hence, to construct the matrix $P,$ we use the eigenvector $\overset{―}{v},$ the complex conjugate of $v.$

Next, we find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{v} & =[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i}\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(\overset{―}{v})}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(\overset{―}{v})}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(\overset{―}{v}) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{v}) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Converting a Matrix to Rotation-Scaling Form Using the Complex Conjugate
content.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2+\text{i} \\ 1-\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3-2\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\ne C,
$$

while

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) \\ -\text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda })\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

So, our rotation-scaling matrix $C$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\overset{―}{\lambda }=3+2\text{i},$ 
 the complex conjugate of $\lambda .$ Hence, to construct the matrix $P,$ we use the eigenvector $\overset{―}{v},$ the complex conjugate of $v.$

Next, we find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{v} & =[\begin{aligned}2-\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i}\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(\overset{―}{v})}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(\overset{―}{v})}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(\overset{―}{v}) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{v}) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1+6\text{i} \\ 8\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1-5\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]\ne C,
$$

while

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) \\ -\text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda })\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

So, our rotation-scaling matrix $C$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\overset{―}{\lambda }=1+5\text{i},$ 
 the complex conjugate of $\lambda .$ Hence, to construct the matrix $P,$ we use the eigenvector $\overset{―}{v},$ the complex conjugate of $v.$

Next, we find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{v} & =[\begin{aligned}-1-6\text{i} \\ 8\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(\overset{―}{v})}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(\overset{―}{v})}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(\overset{―}{v}) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{v}) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -6 \\ 8 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Converting a Matrix to Rotation-Scaling Form Using the Complex Conjugate
content.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1+6\text{i} \\ 8\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1-5\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]\ne C,
$$

while

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) \\ -\text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda })\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

So, our rotation-scaling matrix $C$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\overset{―}{\lambda }=1+5\text{i},$ 
 the complex conjugate of $\lambda .$ Hence, to construct the matrix $P,$ we use the eigenvector $\overset{―}{v},$ the complex conjugate of $v.$

Next, we find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{v} & =[\begin{aligned}-1-6\text{i} \\ 8\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(\overset{―}{v})}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(\overset{―}{v})}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(\overset{―}{v}) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{v}) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -6 \\ 8 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: C corresponds to 7i, the conjugate of the given eigenvalue. Use the conjugate eigenvector (-3-i,2)^T and form P from its real and imaginary parts: P=[[-3,-1],[2,0]]. Its determinant is 2, and AP=PC gives A=PCP^{-1}. Thus option d is correct.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-3+\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 7 \\ -7 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-7\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & -7 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}]\ne C,
$$

while

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) \\ -\text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda })\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 7 \\ -7 & 0\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

So, our rotation-scaling matrix $C$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\overset{―}{\lambda }=7\text{i},$ 
 the complex conjugate of $\lambda .$ Hence, to construct the matrix $P,$ we use the eigenvector $\overset{―}{v},$ the complex conjugate of $v.$

Next, we find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{v} & =[\begin{aligned}-3-\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(\overset{―}{v})}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(\overset{―}{v})}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(\overset{―}{v}) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{v}) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

P=[||Re(v)Im(v)||],C=[Re(λ)Im(λ)−Im(λ)Re(λ)],

and v is an eigenvector of A corresponding to the complex eigenvalue λ.

First, notice that

[Re(λ)Im(λ)−Im(λ)Re(λ)]=[0−770]≠C,

while

[Re(λ―)Im(λ―)−Im(λ―)Re(λ―)]=[07−70]=C.

So, our rotation-scaling matrix C corresponds to the eigenvalue λ―=7i, the complex conjugate of λ. Hence, to construct the matrix P, we use the eigenvector v―, the complex conjugate of v.

Next, we find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

v―=[−3−i2]=[−32]⏟Re(v―)+i[−10]⏟Im(v―)

Finally, we can now construct P:

P=[||Re(v―)Im(v―)||]=[−3−120].

content.knowledge_point: Converting a Matrix to Rotation-Scaling Form Using the Complex Conjugate
content.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-3+\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 7 \\ -7 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-7\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & -7 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}]\ne C,
$$

while

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) \\ -\text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda })\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 7 \\ -7 & 0\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

So, our rotation-scaling matrix $C$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\overset{―}{\lambda }=7\text{i},$ 
 the complex conjugate of $\lambda .$ Hence, to construct the matrix $P,$ we use the eigenvector $\overset{―}{v},$ the complex conjugate of $v.$

Next, we find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{v} & =[\begin{aligned}-3-\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(\overset{―}{v})}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(\overset{―}{v})}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(\overset{―}{v}) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{v}) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-3+2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-4\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\ne C,
$$

while

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) \\ -\text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda })\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

So, our rotation-scaling matrix $C$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\overset{―}{\lambda }=4\text{i},$ 
 the complex conjugate of $\lambda .$ Hence, to construct the matrix $P,$ we use the eigenvector $\overset{―}{v},$ the complex conjugate of $v.$

Next, we find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{v} & =[\begin{aligned}-3-2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(\overset{―}{v})}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(\overset{―}{v})}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(\overset{―}{v}) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{v}) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Converting a Matrix to Rotation-Scaling Form Using the Complex Conjugate
content.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-3+2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-4\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\ne C,
$$

while

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) \\ -\text{Im}(\overset{―}{\lambda }) & \text{Re}(\overset{―}{\lambda })\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

So, our rotation-scaling matrix $C$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\overset{―}{\lambda }=4\text{i},$ 
 the complex conjugate of $\lambda .$ Hence, to construct the matrix $P,$ we use the eigenvector $\overset{―}{v},$ the complex conjugate of $v.$

Next, we find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{v} & =[\begin{aligned}-3-2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(\overset{―}{v})}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(\overset{―}{v})}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(\overset{―}{v}) & \text{Im}(\overset{―}{v}) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
